bib.title: Chapter 14: Use Case: A Multi-Agent System for Loan Processing (in Agentic Architectural Patterns for Building Multi-Agent Systems)

question: How does a monolithic Level 3 single-agent loan processor evolve into a Level 4 hierarchical multi-agent system, and which patterns does that use?
hypothesis: Promoting tools to single-purpose specialist agents under a supervisor fixes the monolith's cognitive overload, single point of failure and lack of specialisation.
contributions: Refactor of the Chapter 13 loan agent into an FCoT supervisor plus four AgentTool-wrapped LlmAgent specialists (google-adk).
Two annotated logs (happy path, denied path).
Mapping of the code to Supervisor, Agent Delegates to Agent, FCoT, Fault Tolerance and Isolation, Modularity, Observability, Explainability and Audit Trail patterns, and to Agentic AI Levels 3-6.

limits: No measurement: no accuracy, latency, token cost, failure rate or comparison with the Chapter 13 monolith; claims of resilience and maintainability are asserted, not tested.
Only two single runs (approved, denied); no tool-failure or sub-agent-error scenario is run, so the fault-isolation and Reflect/Resolve/Escalate policy is untested here.
All tool bodies are elided ('# ... function definition from the notebook ...') and tools are simulated; every score, threshold and applicant is invented.
Logs are excerpted with ellipses and the 'Iteration 1/2' labels are the author's; risk scale and approval threshold are not given.
Chapter itself warns of nested latency and token cost per delegation layer, but gives no figures.
Orchestrator uses contextual state (context window) not a structured state dict; relies on prompt to forward correct fields.
practices: Use the hierarchical Supervisor/Orchestrator topology for regulated workflows needing auditability (p.450).
Give each specialist one tool and a narrow instruction that states its required input, to form a data contract (p.454).
Enforce strict input/output schemas (e.g., Pydantic) in production rather than bare type hints (p.452).
Assign lightweight models (Flash) to simple specialists and stronger ones (Pro) to policy-heavy ones, accepting some behavioural variation (p.454).
Avoid deep delegation chains: each layer adds a full LLM round trip (p.455).
Set temperature 0.0 for analytical specialists, cap max_output_tokens, configure safety_settings via GenerateContentConfig (p.455).
Wrap runs in rate limiting plus exponential-backoff retry on 429 errors (p.456).
Instruct the orchestrator explicitly which fields to extract and forward between agents (p.457).
Log thoughts, tool calls and outputs separately for observability (p.459).

terms.definition: a manager agent plans, delegates sub-tasks to specialists, monitors progress and synthesizes the result
the supervisor delegates work to another autonomous agent; ADK AgentTool encapsulates an agent behind a tool interface
adaptive recursive RECAP -> REASON -> VERIFY loop for planning and synthesis (expansion of FCoT not given in this chapter)
state is the accumulated history of JSON outputs from specialists, held in the context window

problems: Prose and code disagree: Level-3 section says the monolith is 'the quintessential Level 5 system' (p.467) though headed Level 3 and called Level 3 elsewhere.
Level 4 called 'the summit' / 'highest level' (p.467, p.469) yet Levels 5 and 6 are described on p.468.
Prose says 'we rely on the default settings' (p.456) right after code setting thinking_budget=1024; temperature 0.0 advised but not in shown code.
start_agent_run (retry/throttle runner) is defined but call_agent calls runner.run directly, so the guardrail is not shown in use.
Heterogeneous-model advice (Flash vs Pro) but only gemini-3-flash for document_validator is shown; other three agents elided.
Runner is built with agent=agent while the orchestrator variable is never shown being created.
Contextual-state note example uses status 'valid' and CUST-123, the log shows 'validated' and CUST-12345.
Denied-path applicant submits one document (drivers_license.pdf) yet the log says 'the documents looked good'.
Page numbers: footers give book pages 450-470; extraction pages are shifted (Fig 14.1 on book p.451 = PDF p3).
No embedded instructions found; last page is a promo for a newsletter.
